title: Usage profile
description: Monthly consumption for a working pattern. Introduced by QUERIES.md §8.1: every cost answer depends on one, and a cost figure resting on an invented token count is exactly the fabrication CLAUDE.md §1 prohibits. Until Class D experiments run, profiles are 'assumed' with low confidence, and that propagates into every cost result.

status.description: 'measured' requires derived_from pointing at a Class D experiment.

cache_hit_rate.description: Materially changes cost on providers with cache pricing. Frequently the difference between two stacks.

retry_rate.description: Failed and re-run work. A model needing four attempts is not cheap; omitting this is how per-token comparisons mislead.

distribution.description: Usage is not uniform. Percentiles let the engine answer 'at your heavy months' as well as 'typical'.

content_mix.description: ADDED M4.1 (S1). Share of tokens by content type. Tokenizer efficiency varies by content: exp-tokenizer-normalization-v1 found up to 23 points of spread between prose and structured data. A single per-vendor multiplier would be wrong by that margin. Shares should sum to ~1.0; omitted means unknown, NOT uniform.

status.description: Inherits the profile's own status discipline.

assumptions.description: Written out in full and surfaced with every cost figure computed from this profile. Mandatory even when status is 'measured' — measurement conditions are assumptions too.
